messages.author: b5d05cf6ee4e8349
messages.subject: Relationship with a continuing variable
parts:
Hi all

I am wondering how one would go about comparing morphological data with a continuing variable, other than size. Similar as can be done with tpsRegr. I have a number of populations of Arctic charr. I have compared their morphology using the ProcD.lm function. I have then further analysed the data using linear discriminant analysis. I am interested in creating deformation grids at the extreme of my discriminant axis's and add that to the plot. I can do this in tpsRegr, and add this using backwoods methods, e.g. in powerpoint. But I would be interested in doing this in R. Similarly one might be interested in other continuing variables to compare to shape, e.g. analyzing fork length, instead of centroid size, or environmental factors, e.g. temperature across populations etc. 

I was wondering if the plotAllometry function could be used or if there are some other tricks to approach this. 

Thank you in advance

Bjarni

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Relationship with a continuing variable
parts:
Bjarni,

Please read the help page shape.predictor. This function, in combination with plotRefToTaregt is designed to accomplish exactly your objective.

Cheers!
Mike
